lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Nilda, this is Marcus. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the drinks on the weekend going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've always eaten late, that's how we do it at home.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Having a glass of water between drinks is an easy way to slow down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can stick to two beers if I eat first.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Having a glass of water between drinks is an easy way to slow down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you drink mostly on weekends?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You said the same thing last week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everybody keeps telling me that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Having a glass of water between drinks is an easy way to slow down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You think you can do it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Let's say I keep it to 3 drinks on the weekend.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll ask my son to come with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Nilda. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Marcus. Bye!

tags.note: Water-between-drinks tip repeated verbatim; see flags
Same water tip repeated a third time
Points out repeated statement; confrontational, not reflective

flags.reason: Same water-between-drinks suggestion given without permission or response to client, repeated at lines 14 and 23.
Pointing out she said the same thing last week shifts toward confronting rather than exploring her ambivalence.
Client offered a concrete plan (two beers after eating); coach did not reflect or build on it.
Client stated a personal reason for change ('for my head too'); coach did not reflect it and instead moved to a persuasive comment.
Client expressed self-efficacy ('I know I can do it'); reflection was minimal and no elaboration was invited.

score.summary: Marcus asked permission and offered autonomy at points, and he helped Nilda set a concrete weekend goal and plan for barriers. However, he repeated the same water tip three times without responding to her replies and missed several change-talk statements, so the session leaned toward advice-giving.
strengths: Line 5 and 22: affirmed Nilda's control over her choices and kept the decision with her.
Line 27-29: asked open questions to set a goal and identify a barrier, which drew out her own plan.
Line 33: closed warmly with specific encouragement.
coaching_tips: Line 10, 14, 23: the water tip was repeated verbatim; after one offer, reflect her response instead of repeating it.
Line 20: instead of pointing out the repeat, try a complex reflection such as 'Part of you wants this for your head as well as your body, and part of you is tired of hearing it.'
Line 11 and 15: reflect her concrete plans ('So two beers after eating, and a reminder on the fridge') to strengthen change talk.
Line 24: try 'What makes you confident you can do it?' to draw out her self-efficacy.
